title: Design semi-structured and unstructured data storage
learningObjective: Recommend storage for semi-structured data (Cosmos DB APIs, Table Storage) and unstructured data (Blob Storage, Data Lake Storage, Azure Files, Azure NetApp Files).
foundation: Semi-structured data has a shape but not fixed columns: JSON documents, key-value pairs, graphs. Unstructured data is files and objects: images, videos, backups.
Azure Cosmos DB stores semi-structured data with low latency anywhere in the world. Blob Storage stores any amount of files cheaply.
engineer: Cosmos DB: choose the API by app needs: NoSQL (native, newest features), MongoDB (RU-based or vCore-based; keep MongoDB drivers), Apache Cassandra, Apache Gremlin (graph), Table (Table Storage compatible, with global distribution and secondary indexes) and PostgreSQL (distributed relational). Design the partition key for high cardinality and even distribution; choose provisioned throughput (manual or autoscale) or serverless; set the consistency level (strong, bounded staleness, session (default), consistent prefix, eventual); add regions and optionally multi-region writes.
Azure Table Storage: simple key-value storage inside a storage account, cheapest option, without global distribution or latency SLAs.

Unstructured: Blob Storage (block blobs for files, append blobs for logs, page blobs for VHDs), Data Lake Storage (hierarchical namespace: real directories, POSIX ACLs, analytics engines), Azure Files (SMB and NFS shares, identity-based access, Azure File Sync), Azure NetApp Files (enterprise NAS with sub-millisecond latency for SAP HANA, HPC and databases), and Azure Managed Lustre for HPC scratch.

example.title: A global retail platform
body: The product catalogue and shopping carts use Cosmos DB for NoSQL with /tenantId as partition key, in three regions with session consistency. A recommendation graph uses the Gremlin API.
Product images live in Blob Storage, the analytics lake uses Data Lake Storage, store file shares move to Azure Files, and the SAP HANA system uses Azure NetApp Files.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: Create Azure Cosmos DB account: choose API, capacity mode, regions, multi-region writes.
Storage account > Advanced: Enable hierarchical namespace (Data Lake Storage).
Azure NetApp Files: create a NetApp account, capacity pool (service level) and volume.
configuration.cli:
az cosmosdb create -g rg-data -n cosmos-retail --locations regionName=westeurope failoverPriority=0 --locations regionName=eastus failoverPriority=1 --default-consistency-level Session
az storage account create -g rg-data -n stlakeretail --sku Standard_ZRS --kind StorageV2 --hns true

troubleshooting.symptom: Cosmos DB requests are throttled (429) on one partition while others are idle.
troubleshooting.cause: Hot partition from a low-cardinality key.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose a high-cardinality partition key (or hierarchical partition keys).

troubleshooting.symptom: Spark jobs on blob storage are slow when renaming folders.
troubleshooting.cause: Flat namespace: folder rename copies every blob.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Data Lake Storage (hierarchical namespace) for analytics.

comparisons.service: Cosmos DB Table API vs Table Storage
comparisons.difference: Cosmos adds global distribution, latency SLAs and automatic indexing at higher cost.
Files: general-purpose shares; NetApp Files: high-performance enterprise workloads.

misconceptions.myth: Cosmos DB is only for NoSQL documents.
misconceptions.reality: It offers several APIs, including MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin and PostgreSQL.
It increases latency and limits availability; session is the default for good reason.

architectureDecisions: Cosmos DB API by app need; partition key by cardinality.
Table Storage when cheap and simple is enough.
Blob for objects, Data Lake for analytics, Files for shares, NetApp Files for enterprise NAS.

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: Not everything fits in tables
body: Shopping carts are JSON, device settings are key-values, and there are millions of images and huge analytics files.

steps.label: Cosmos DB
steps.title: Semi-structured, low latency, global
body: Pick the API your app speaks (NoSQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table). Choose a partition key with many distinct values so load spreads evenly. Session consistency is the sensible default.

callout.text: A bad partition key causes throttling on one hot partition.

steps.label: Table
steps.title: When cheap and simple wins
body: Table Storage keeps key-value data in a storage account at very low cost, without global distribution.

steps.label: Files and objects
steps.title: Four unstructured stores
body: Blob: objects at any scale. Data Lake Storage: blob with real folders and ACLs for analytics. Azure Files: SMB/NFS shares. Azure NetApp Files: very fast enterprise NAS for SAP, HPC and databases.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Non-relational design
recap: Cosmos DB: API by app, high-cardinality partition key
Blob / Data Lake / Files / NetApp Files
